fronts.name: descriptor capability gate
fronts.finding: The prior capability gate was insufficient for descriptor-relative name custody because it did not require stat(..., dir_fd=..., follow_symlinks=False). The gate and regression source now require both stat capabilities.

fronts.name: held-directory descriptor custody
fronts.finding: A held O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW root descriptor now anchors bounded descriptor-relative enumeration/open/stat source work. Code-first review caught a directory-stream-position wound in the first draft, so each inventory scan now opens a fresh '.' directory handle relative to the held authority root. This strengthens root custody after descriptor acquisition without proving universal filesystem atomicity, candidate swap-and-restore immunity, identity-reuse immunity, or canonical v10 owner integration.

fronts.name: current inventory exact grammar
fronts.finding: The actual patches/ inventory now has a repository-level v10 admission regression requiring evidenceComplete with no discovery errors and keeping historical/applied v8/v9/v10 custody artifacts out of promotion authority. Source existence is not a successful inventory audit.

fronts.name: warm wall / skill harvest
fronts.finding: The existing custody wall now distinguishes portable v10 pathname revalidation from descriptor-bound supporting source, and a dedicated descriptor-custody skill preserves the exact capability membrane and the scan-position correction scar.

reviewScars: Passing the held authority descriptor directly to repeated scandir calls was rejected; each bounded scan now gets a fresh descriptor-relative directory handle so inventory results do not depend on prior stream position.
Descriptor-bound root custody is stronger than pathname pre/post revalidation but does not make candidate-name content observations atomic.
The new POSIX source is unexecuted; platform/API behavior remains source-level until an authorized test receipt exists.
